description: Who you write for. The score is the Developer Trust filter (config/grader-prompt.md); these objectives tell the grader who's reading, and appear in the panel's "Serving" select. Edit them in the extension's options page. This file is an example: replace it with your own.

objectives.statement: Build credibility as a developer-ecosystem leader who measures outcomes.
objectives.audience: DevRel and developer-experience leaders, platform product and engineering leaders.
proof_that_counts: A program you ran, with a real number
A framework that separates two things people conflate
A metric you use or would use (first-attempt success, integrations retained)
A failure and what fixed it
not_this: hot takes with no program behind them

objectives.statement: Build credibility as a hands-on agent builder.
objectives.audience: Advanced AI prototypers and engineers shipping agents.
proof_that_counts: Something you shipped: a repo, a demo clip, a screenshot
A result from a real run, with the number
What broke and how you fixed it
An exact prompt, config or setup someone can copy
in_scope: Claude Code and MCP in practice
not_this: commentary on other people's launches without trying them

objectives.statement: Build credibility on how agents change developer adoption.
objectives.audience: Both groups above: the bridge between DevRel leaders and agent builders.
proof_that_counts: A test the reader can run this afternoon
A research read with a practical so-what
A concrete change to docs, onboarding or measurement for a non-human reader
in_scope: docs legible to models, llms.txt, MCP tool definitions
measurement when the reader isn't human
the 'DevRel in the Agent Era' series

off_objective_everywhere: Personal life, relationships, housing, legal matters
Reacting to news without adding proof

scoring.note: The score is the Developer Trust filter in config/grader-prompt.md (0-10; Post unlocks at 8.0). Objectives are context for who's reading; they don't change the score.
